The proposed project consists of embankment repairs at at three identified bank failure locations along a streamside easement road that travels alongside Sheephouse Creek through the Keller property. The road provides primary year- round access to the Riciloi residence, and the Project is designed to enhance riparian habitat, reduce future sediment delivery, and restore and protect the structural integrity of stream banks where the unpaved access road is vulnerable to collapse along the left bank of Sheephouse Creek. The project proposes boulder-ballasted wood structures (logs and logs with rootwads) that will act as bank-stabilization, energy dissipation, and in-stream habitat features. This design will meet project objectives by improving shallow water habitat and increasing the availability of velocity refugia for aquatic organisms, stabilizing streambanks and preventing large loads of fine sediment from polluting the stream system, preserving the natural aesthetic and restoring important fluvial geomorphic processes of Sheephouse Creek, as well as protecting and rebuilding portions of the easement road using a “no net fill” approach to avoid increasing flood risk.

AllStarz Pumping & Engineering will be performing the decommissioning and proper abandonment of the existing septic system located at the above- referenced property. The following scope outlines the full procedure we will undertake to comply with county and environmental regulations: 1. Expose Existing Septic Tanks Our crew will excavate and fully expose all existing septic tanks on site using appropriate equipment. All necessary precautions will be taken to avoid disturbing any nearby utilities, structures, or vegetation. 2. Pumping and Cleaning (if necessary) If any sewage, sludge, or liquid remains in the tanks, we will arrange for a licensed septic pumper to remove and legally dispose of the contents at an approved facility. 3. Perforation of Tank Bottoms After the tanks are emptied, we will puncture holes in the bottom of each tank to ensure proper drainage and prevent future water accumulation. 4. Collapse of Tanks The tanks will then be crushed and collapsed in place to reduce the potential for future ground settling or void formation. 5. Fill With Clean Crushed Rock The interior of each collapsed tank will be filled with clean, drainable crushed rock to stabilize the structure and maintain subsurface drainage. 6. Backfill and Compaction The excavation area will then be backfilled with a mixture of compacted gravel and clean native soil (or imported fill, if needed). Material will be placed and compacted in lifts to minimize future settling. 7. Final Grading The area will be finish-graded to restore natural contours and to promote positive surface drainage away from all structures.
